articles.title: Hallux Valgus, Not Hallux Abductus Valgus: A Short Report on Historical and Anatomical Terminology.
articles.authors: Dalmau-Pastor M, Errichiello C, Miller CP, Marcarelli M, Germano M, Del Vecchio JJ
articles.outcomes: Clarification that hallux valgus (not hallux abductus valgus) is the anatomically correct term for the deformity involving lateral deviation of the great toe and medial deviation of the first metatarsal
articles.take_home: The common term hallux abductus valgus is anatomically incorrect because the adductor muscle, not the abductor muscle, contributes to the deformity. The authors recommend using hallux valgus as the correct terminology.

articles.title: Outcomes of Iliac Crest Bone-Block Arthrodesis After Failed First MTP Joint Surgery With Bone Loss.
articles.authors: Manti N, Atalay M, Ulgen NK, Akkurt MO, Erginoglu SE, Oznur A
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision surgery for failed first metatarsophalangeal joint surgery with bone loss
articles.sample_size: 72 patients with minimum 2 years follow-up (83.3% had at least 3 years)
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union rates, fusion success, complications, pain (VAS score), quality of life (SF-36 score)
articles.take_home: This salvage operation using bone graft from the pelvis successfully fused the big toe joint in 97% of patients after previous failed surgery, with pain reducing from severe to minimal. However, nearly half of patients experienced complications, and those with other health conditions or larger bone defects had less good outcomes.

articles.title: Dedicated Ankle AP and Long-Leg Radiographs Are Not Interchangeable for Assessing Coronal Ankle Alignment: A Weightbearing CT-Based Comparison.
articles.authors: Kim J, Ward L, Voellmicke I, Garibaldi R, Ellis SJ, Demetracopoulos CA, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent long-leg radiographs, dedicated ankle radiographs, and weightbearing CT scans of the ankle within 6 months
articles.outcomes: Coronal ankle alignment measurements including medial distal tibial angle and talar tilt, compared between long-leg radiographs and dedicated ankle AP radiographs using weightbearing CT as reference
articles.take_home: Long-leg radiographs and dedicated ankle radiographs give different measurements of ankle alignment and should not be used interchangeably. The study found that in about one in five ankles, the two imaging methods disagreed about whether the ankle was tilted inward or outward, so using the wrong radiograph type could lead to incorrect assessment of ankle deformity.

articles.title: Obesity Is Associated With Earlier Mechanical Failure Following Total Ankle Arthroplasty Independent of Tibial Stem or Keel Augmentation.
articles.authors: Sommi C, Thomas GM, McCahon JAS, Dowd T, Hsu A, Parekh SG, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total ankle arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mechanical failure requiring revision of metal components; patient-reported outcomes (FAAM-ADL and VAS pain scores)
articles.take_home: Patients with a BMI of 30 or above had more than twice the risk of mechanical failure of their ankle replacement compared to those with lower BMI, regardless of whether the implant had extra fixation features. Using implants with stems or keels did not prevent earlier failure in obese patients.

articles.title: The Superior Fascicle of the Anterior Talofibular Ligament Functions as a Restraint Against Internal Rotation: A Cadaveric Biomechanical Study.
articles.authors: Koyama T, Teramoto A, Mori Y, Murahashi Y, Takahashi K, Ueda N, et al.
articles.outcomes: Internal rotation displacement, anterior talar translation, inversion angles, and in situ forces under loading at different ankle positions
articles.take_home: Complete injury to the superior part of the front ankle ligament causes the ankle to rotate inward more than normal, but partial injuries do not. This suggests doctors should test for internal rotation when checking for this type of ankle ligament injury.

articles.title: Prosthetic Joint Infection After Total Ankle Arthroplasty: A Propensity-Matched Analysis of Risk Factors and Outcomes.
articles.authors: McCahon JAS, Thomas GM, Sherman M, Hsu A, O'Neil J, Parekh SG, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total ankle replacement
articles.sample_size: 1008 primary ankle replacements; 27 with prosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Infection rate, risk factors for infection, microbiologic profiles, surgical management strategies, limb salvage rate, prosthesis retention rate
articles.take_home: Prosthetic joint infection after ankle replacement occurred in 2.7% of cases, with doing an additional bone procedure on the heel bone identified as a major risk factor. Despite this serious complication, most patients kept their leg and their replacement prosthesis worked, with over 96% avoiding amputation.

articles.title: Age-Related Differences in Postoperative Outcomes After Arthroscopic Lateral Ligament Repair for Chronic Lateral Ankle Instability.
articles.authors: Moriwaki D, Yeo SY, Jujo Y, Nakasa T, Adachi N, Takao M
articles.population: Patients with chronic lateral ankle instability undergoing arthroscopic lateral ligament repair
articles.sample_size: 934 patients across five age groups (skeletally immature, adolescents, young adults, middle-aged, elderly)
articles.outcomes: Self-Administered Foot Evaluation Questionnaire (SAFE-Q) scores at one year; time to free gait, jogging, and return to full sports activities
articles.take_home: Younger patients recovered faster and reported better physical and social functioning after surgery, but older patients still improved significantly and should not be excluded from the procedure based on age alone.

articles.title: Suture Button Syndesmosis Repair Augmented With Nonanatomic vs Anatomic AITFL Reconstruction and the Added Effect of Deltoid Repair: A Cadaveric Biomechanical Study.
articles.authors: Carlson MR, Shoemaker EP, Chen C, Donaghue PH, Moen RK, Coetzee JC, et al.
articles.outcomes: Ankle external and internal rotation stability under mechanical testing with various surgical repair constructs
articles.take_home: Adding ligament repairs to suture button syndesmosis fixation improved ankle stability, with both AITFL reconstruction methods performing similarly and deltoid repair providing additional medial stability. However, no repair technique fully restored the ankle to its native state.

articles.title: Development and Internal Validation of a Predictive Model for Clinically Meaningful AOS Improvement After Primary Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Albarran CF, Koolen M, Trache T, Alharbi SK, Veljkovic A, Gagne O, et al.
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with internal validation
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total ankle replacement for ankle osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Clinically meaningful improvement in ankle disability defined as 28 or more points improvement on the Ankle Osteoarthritis Scale between pre-operative and 1-2 year follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with higher baseline ankle disability and instability as the cause of their arthritis were more likely to experience significant improvement after ankle replacement. A baseline disability score above 63 was associated with a good chance of meaningful improvement.

articles.title: Anterior cruciate ligament resection has no clinical effect on mediolateral gap laxity assessment in robotic-assisted total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Leggieri F, Grant S, Wood JA, Sergis N, Wernecke GC, Chen DB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Mediolateral laxity gap measurements in extension and flexion before and after anterior cruciate ligament resection
articles.take_home: Removing the anterior cruciate ligament during robotic-assisted knee replacement does not meaningfully change measurements used to position the new joint, suggesting it may not be necessary to routinely remove this ligament when taking these measurements.

articles.title: Quantitative Bone SPECT/CT in Varus-Type Ankle Osteoarthritis: Association With Radiographic Stage and Preoperative Pain.
articles.authors: Shimokawa K, Matsubara H, Shibutani T, Kayano D, Nakazawa Y, Yoneyama H, et al.
articles.outcomes: Quantitative bone SPECT/CT parameters (SUVmax, SUVpeak, total bone uptake) associated with radiographic stage and preoperative pain severity (visual analogue scale)
articles.take_home: Bone SPECT/CT scans showed increased radiotracer uptake with more advanced ankle osteoarthritis, and this uptake had moderate correlation with patients' pain levels. These findings suggest this imaging technique could be useful alongside standard X-rays to assess ankle osteoarthritis, although more research is needed.

articles.title: Malnutrition is associated with poor outcomes following total ankle arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Sommi C, Thomas GM, O'Mara L, Pedowitz DI, Parekh SG, Dowd T
articles.outcomes: Short-term medical complications within 90 days (readmission, wound disruption, sepsis, myocardial infarction, pulmonary embolism, pneumonia, deep vein thrombosis, infection) and long-term mechanical outcomes at 5 years (periprosthetic joint infection, revision arthrodesis, periprosthetic fracture, below knee amputation)
articles.take_home: Patients with signs of malnutrition before ankle replacement surgery had significantly more complications within 90 days and at 5 years, including serious infections and the need for further surgery. Improving nutrition markers before surgery could be a way to reduce these poor outcomes.
